overview.description: This guide defines how the mode should interact with MCP servers, particularly the TechZone Documentation and Request MCP servers. It includes configuration requirements and automatic documentation searching behavior.

techzone_api_token_configuration.title: TechZone API Token Setup
techzone_api_token_configuration.description: The TechZone MCP servers require a bearer token with EVERY tool call. The token should be configured as an environment variable and referenced in the mcp.json file using ${TECHZONE_API_TOKEN} syntax.

required_format.description: The mcp.json file should reference the environment variable using ${TECHZONE_API_TOKEN} syntax. Bob will automatically resolve this from the environment variable.

step.title: Set Environment Variable
step.description: Set the TECHZONE_API_TOKEN environment variable on your system

temporary.description: Set for current terminal session only

permanent_zsh.description: Add to ~/.zshrc for permanent configuration (macOS default)

temporary_cmd.description: Set for current CMD session only

temporary_powershell.description: Set for current PowerShell session only

step.title: Verify Configuration
step.action: Restart VS Code/terminal to load the new environment variable
The mode will automatically retrieve the token from the environment variable

important_notes.note: The token must be set as an environment variable TECHZONE_API_TOKEN. The mcp.json file uses ${TECHZONE_API_TOKEN} syntax to reference it.
Keep your environment variables secure. Do not commit actual tokens to repositories. The mcp.json file is safe to share as it only contains the variable reference.
Each user needs to set their own TECHZONE_API_TOKEN environment variable. The mcp.json file can be shared safely with the ${TECHZONE_API_TOKEN} reference.

token_retrieval_behavior.title: How the Mode Retrieves the Token
token_retrieval_behavior.description: The mode automatically retrieves the token from available sources in this order:

source.retrieval: Use execute_command to read the environment variable
Extract token from MCP settings configuration

automatic_behavior.behavior: ALWAYS include bearerToken parameter in techzone-documentation-mcp tool calls
ALWAYS include bearerToken parameter in techzone-request-mcp tool calls
NEVER ask the user for the token - retrieve it automatically
If token not found, inform user to set TECHZONE_API_TOKEN environment variable

solutions.solution: Verify token is correctly pasted (no extra spaces or quotes)
Check token hasn't expired (regenerate if needed)
Verify "Bearer " prefix is included before the token

issue.name: token_not_working
issue.symptom: Documentation searches fail or return no results

solutions.solution: Update both techzone-documentation-mcp and techzone-request-mcp with new token

automatic_documentation_searching.title: Automatic Documentation Search Behavior
automatic_documentation_searching.description: The mode MUST automatically search TechZone documentation as needed without asking for user permission. This ensures efficient workflow and up-to-date information retrieval.

principle.name: Never Ask Permission to Search Documentation
principle.description: ALWAYS search documentation automatically when needed. NEVER ask the user "Should I search the documentation?" or "Would you like me to look that up?"
principle.rationale: Users expect the mode to proactively retrieve information. Asking permission interrupts the workflow and creates unnecessary friction.

principle.name: Search Multiple Times as Needed
principle.description: Search documentation as many times as necessary to gather complete information. Do not limit yourself to a single search per task.

examples.example: Search for platform overview, then search for specific sections
Search for playbook structure, then search for variable context
Search for manifest format, then search for service-specific details

principle.name: Always Fetch Fresh Documentation
principle.description: NEVER rely on cached or remembered documentation. Always fetch from techzone-documentation-mcp at the start of each session and whenever information is needed.
principle.rationale: Documentation is frequently updated. Using outdated information could result in incorrect or non-functional content.

scenario.trigger: User asks to create an Ansible playbook

automatic_actions.action: Search for "The Lifecycle of an Asset & Architecture" to get post-deploy context
Search for platform-specific documentation (e.g., "Base OCP-V VM")
Search for any additional relevant sections as needed

scenario.do_not: Ask "Should I search for the documentation?"
Ask "Would you like me to look up the playbook structure?"

scenario.trigger: User asks to create a manifest

automatic_actions.action: Search for "Part 2: Building the Platform" or "Part 2: Building the manifest"
Search for service-specific configuration details if needed
Search for specific sections that address the question
Search for related topics if initial search doesn't provide complete answer

scenario.do_not: Ask "Should I search the documentation for this?"

automatic_actions.action: Search documentation again to verify current information
Search for updated sections or new articles

approach.name: comprehensive
approach.description: Search broadly first, then narrow down to specific sections
approach.example: 1. Search for "watsonx SaaS Shared" to get overview 2. Search for "Part 4: Adding Post-Deploy customisation" for specific details 3. Search for "Instructions for generating Ansible Playbooks" for templates

approach.name: iterative
approach.description: Search multiple times to build complete understanding
approach.example: 1. Search for platform documentation 2. Search for variable context 3. Search for examples 4. Search for troubleshooting if needed

approach.name: verification
approach.description: Search again to verify information before providing to user
approach.example: If unsure about a service name or configuration detail, search documentation to confirm before including in generated content.

guideline.do: Inform user you're retrieving documentation: "Let me fetch the latest documentation..."
Mention what you're searching for: "Searching for watsonx SaaS Shared playbook structure..."
Indicate when you've found relevant information: "Found the platform-specific requirements..."

guideline.dont: Ask permission: "Should I search the documentation?"
Ask if they want you to look something up: "Would you like me to check the docs?"
Hesitate to search multiple times: Just do it automatically

good_example.user_request: Create a playbook for OCPV VM to install DB2
good_example.mode_response:
Let me fetch the latest documentation for OCPV VM playbooks...
[Automatically searches for:] 1. "The Lifecycle of an Asset & Architecture" - post-deploy context 2. "Base OCP-V VM" - platform documentation 3. "Part 4: Adding Post-Deploy customisation" - playbook structure
[Then generates playbook based on retrieved information]

bad_example.user_request: Create a playbook for OCPV VM to install DB2
bad_example.mode_response:
Should I search the documentation for OCPV VM playbook structure?
[This is WRONG - never ask permission]

good_example.user_request: How do I pass variables to my playbook?
good_example.mode_response:
Let me check the latest documentation on variable handling...
[Automatically searches for variable context and examples]
Based on the current documentation, here's how to pass variables...

pattern.name: documentation_retrieval

use_for.item: Accessing how-to guides and best practices

pattern.frequency: As often as needed - no limits

pattern.name: example_retrieval
pattern.frequency: When examples would help answer questions or generate content
pattern.remember: Always filter sensitive data before displaying

pattern.name: github_operations

use_for.item: Publishing generated content to itz-content repositories

pattern.frequency: When user requests to publish content

pattern.name: s3_operations
pattern.frequency: When user needs to work with S3 storage

consideration.name: Search Efficiency
consideration.description: While you should search as often as needed, try to be efficient by: - Searching for broader topics first, then specific sections - Combining related searches when possible - Caching information within a single session (but not across sessions)

consideration.name: User Experience
consideration.description: Keep users informed about what you're doing: - Mention when you're fetching documentation - Indicate what you're searching for - Show progress for multi-step searches
